description: A Director of People must decide whether to approve a six-week protected-focus pilot for a department and define the coordination practices that will keep the pilot from worsening interpersonal handoff problems.

shared_context.S1: The department is considering a six-week protected-focus pilot in which one weekday would have no recurring internal meetings.
shared_context.S2: The pilot would affect the department's recurring meeting calendar and its expectations for handoffs between teams.
shared_context.S3: Some employees want longer uninterrupted work periods, while others are concerned that fewer live touchpoints could make coordination less respectful and less reliable.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the final decision, and the department's normal consultation practice is for the team lead and employee representative to report relevant constraints and observed collaboration problems before Elena closes the decision.

PF1.text: Samir has been experiencing burnout symptoms and told a colleague that keeping Wednesday free of recurring meetings is necessary for him to remain sustainably effective. On that Wednesday focus day, he needs asynchronous work capped at no more than 2 hours before a mandatory break; he has not raised this with Elena because he expected his manager to handle the scheduling concern.

PF2.text: Tessa personally observed exactly four recent handoff misunderstandings caused by missing context in chat, and the affected employees agreed that the pilot needs a Thursday handoff lasting exactly 15 minutes and using a shared written template; this was not added to the proposal because the incidents were handled informally.

acceptance_conditions: The protected-focus pilot must be approved.
Wednesday must be the protected focus day.
The pilot must last exactly six weeks.
Asynchronous work on the focus day must be capped at no more than 2 hours before a mandatory break, and recurring internal meetings must be prohibited that day.
The handoff must occur on Thursday, last exactly 15 minutes, and use a shared written template.
The handoff problem must be documented as exactly four incidents.
A commitment implementing the written handoff protocol must be logged.

content_checks.C5: decisions['handoff_day'] == 'Thursday' and decisions['handoff_duration_minutes'] == 15 and decisions['handoff_uses_shared_template'] == True
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'pilot_safeguard' or c['type'] == 'process' or c['type'] == 'handoff_monitoring' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Samir's sustainability requirement changes the pilot to an approved Wednesday pilot lasting exactly six weeks, with recurring meetings prohibited and asynchronous work capped at exactly 2 hours before a mandatory break.

Tessa's observed record changes the documented incident count to exactly four and requires a Thursday handoff lasting exactly 15 minutes with a shared written template plus an implementation commitment.
